doc.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Seven careers and a deferred question on broadcasting
summary: Schwartz tries to list Schuller's careers and asks about broadcasting; Schuller postpones that subject.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Gunther, what I wanted to interject is to take a giant leap and leave the chronological stuff that we can go back to and come back to. But earlier you mentioned the seven aspects of your career. On my own, I had written down composer, conductor, broadcaster, writer, educator, arranger. So I’m missing one. But I wanted to go back to . . .
There’s one of those I didn’t even include.
The third one. What was the third one?
Broadcaster. That’s the one I want . . .
I did a lot of broadcasting in New York.
That’s what I wanted to go back and talk to you about, because you had mentioned hearing this music on the radio, and I know that in the ’50s you and Nat Hentoff had co-hosted a program.
Yeah, but I also had parallel to that a classical music program, every week for three years.
I’d love to have you talk about that.
Can I come to that a little bit later?
